concepts.title: Similar Figures and Similarity Criteria
concepts.definition: Two figures are similar when they have the same shape but not necessarily the same size; two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are equal (AA) or if corresponding sides are proportional (SSS), or both (SAS).
concepts.key_idea: Same shape, any size: equal angles or proportional sides prove similarity.

solution_steps.explain: Two pairs of equal angles give AA similarity.
Equal ratios of corresponding sides give SSS similarity.
One equal angle pair plus proportional adjacent sides gives SAS.

concepts.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)
concepts.definition: A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio; conversely, a line dividing two sides in the same ratio is parallel to the third side.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel cuts proportionally: the two segments on each side keep one ratio.

concepts.title: Areas of Similar Triangles
concepts.definition: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides - doubling every side quadruples the area.
concepts.key_idea: Sides scale by s, areas scale by s squared - the square is the surprise.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh106.txt section 6.4 (areas of two similar triangles)

solution_steps.explain: The area ratio is the square of the side scale s.

concepts.title: Pythagoras Theorem
concepts.definition: In a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides; its converse identifies right triangles, and both follow from similarity of the triangles formed by the altitude to the hypotenuse.
concepts.key_idea: Right angle forces the relation: hypotenuse squared is the sum of the leg squares.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh106.txt section 6.5 (Pythagoras theorem and its converse)
